verdicts.quote: “Both basic and bearer authentication are supported.”
verdicts.reason: OAuth2 applies to the Aura management API, but the core database/Query API that an agent would use to run Cypher operates with Basic (or bearer) auth; there is no public end-user OAuth consent flow. For a multi-tenant toolkit acting on a customer’s database, Basic is the primary mechanism. ([neo4j.com](https://neo4j.com/docs/query-api/current/authentication-authorization/?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “All tiers can create Aura API credentials.”
verdicts.reason: Credentials are self-serve and available on Free; no partner/app review is required to obtain working API creds. ([neo4j.com](https://neo4j.com/docs/aura/api/authentication/?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “Customers can: Create, Destroy, View, Edit, Pause, Resume, Snapshot, and Restore instances.”
verdicts.reason: The Aura API covers many management capabilities (instances, lifecycle ops, snapshots, etc.), and subsequent additions include user-management endpoints at org/project levels, indicating wide coverage across the product. ([neo4j-aura.canny.io](https://neo4j-aura.canny.io/changelog/aura-api-now-available-for-self-serve-customers?utm_source=openai))

Neo4j publishes and maintains an official MCP server (also documented at neo4j.com/docs/mcp and in the neo4j/mcp GitHub repo). ([neo4j.com](https://neo4j.com/developer/genai-ecosystem/model-context-protocol-mcp/?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “AuraDB Free … get a rate limit of 25 requests per minute.”
verdicts.reason: It’s buildable today with self-serve creds and docs, but you must handle Free-tier rate limits and two auth surfaces (OAuth2 for Aura management; Basic/Bearer for database queries). ([neo4j.com](https://neo4j.com/docs/aura//api/overview/))
